answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity costly in a superlinear way: each new agent must lock collateral, and the required bond rises with the square of how many agents one controller already runs. An honest agent is a single lantern lighting one corner of the market, while a fake army is a river of clones that each demand payment. Because the price grows quadratically, doubling the sybils more than doubles the attacker's bill, so piling up a dune of phantom accounts turns unprofitable before it can swing any vote.
